fields.AN_Notes: Reflexive thematic analysis of FAccT and AIES papers engaging with intersectionality, with an evaluation workshop and survey among AI experts; result are five themes of actionable recommendations. Bias and injustice are determined through Young's definition of social justice. fields.AN_Notes: Conceptual article on algorithmic decision-making (ADM) in social work with case studies (Allegheny Family Screening Tool, COMPAS, NDIS, HEALER, Heat List) and a proposed technical-critical pedagogy. Bias axes from the case studies: race (COMPAS error rates, over-policing through the Heat List), disability (practitioner bias towards children with a disability that the AFST may counter; NDIS needs assessment) and socioeconomic disadvantage (conclusion on groups with social-economic disadvantage, AFST rent and school attendance variables). Harm types: a racially different false-negative rate (Disparate_Performance) and disadvantage through proxy variables such as proximity to known shooters, producing over-policing of African-American communities, together with AFST predictions based on invalid correlations (Indirect_Discrimination). Mitigation: critical, case-based social work education, mandatory interpretative screening and human review (Organisational_Process); Demonstrated because the authors report applying the case-study method in their own undergraduate teaching, without an evaluation of its effect on bias. Gender appears only as misogyny in an enumeration. Bias is not defined; the understanding follows from structural inequality and non-discrimination framing. Theory reference: critical theories of unequal social power and critical race theory frame the treatment of bias in the pedagogy. Studientyp Konzept for the proposed curriculum approach.

fields.AN_Notes: Prompting is the benchmarking instrument (5-shot prompts) and the evaluated mitigation; the work concludes that prompting can serve as an effective mitigation, so Recommended_Practice is also coded. Techniques: few-shot examples with anti-stereotypical invented Winograd sentences (ICL), chain-of-thought prompts including the schematic short variant and the phrase 'Proceed step by step' (Thought_Generation), and a context-supplying system instruction (General_Guidance), verbatim: 'Translate the following sentence from English to Catalan while mitigating gender bias.' followed by the instruction to 'ensure fair gender treatment in the output'. Evaluated: the work's own experiment on Llama-2-7B-chat; the top prompt (invented anti-stereotypical Winograd 5-shot plus short chain-of-thought) raised WinoMT gender accuracy markedly and reduced bias on Gold BUG and less on MuST-SHE, at a slight loss of translation quality; context on gender bias or MuST-SHE examples alone gave no improvement (Sections 6.2, 7, 8). KI_Sonstige teilweise for the neural machine translation baselines. AN_Task Other_Task: machine translation English to Catalan and Spanish. Harm types: correlation with pro-stereotypical sets (Stereotyping), male default without gender cues (Exclusionary_Norms), lower female F1 and the male-female accuracy gap Delta G (Disparate_Performance). Gender is analysed only as binary male/female, stated in the ethical statement; the work defines gender bias but not gender. Friedman and Nissenbaum and the representational/allocational distinction are cited to motivate the definition and do not frame the analysis as theory.

fields.AN_Notes: Theoretical chapter in feminist STS with workforce statistics and the authors' own platform count; no generative AI or prompting focus. fields.AN_Notes: Survey with a taxonomy of intersectional fairness notions and mitigation methods for classification, ranking and NLP. Bias axes: gender and race as the work's own worked example (Black women, Figure 1), coded Intersectional because the argument depends on the combination; further axes appear only in cited applications and dataset tables and are not coded. Harm types: accuracy and worst-case performance differences between subgroups (Disparate_Performance). The surveyed fairness notions also concern allocational outcome disparities (statistical parity, the 80 percent rule), but the work does not classify them as direct or indirect discrimination, so neither code is assigned. Mitigation stages from the synthesised taxonomy: inclusive dataset creation and coverage (Pre_Processing), in-processing methods such as distributionally robust optimisation and adversarial reweighting (In_Training), multicalibration boosting and prediction flipping (Post_Processing), auditing and stakeholder involvement (Organisational_Process). Evaluated is a synthesised evaluation, not the survey's own experiment, and is limited to the reviewed in-processing Max-Min methods and the evaluation of debiasing techniques by Subramanian et al. (gerrymandering of independent-group debiasing); the survey states that most intersectional notions lack real-world evidence. Bias is determined through formal fairness criteria and the legal four-fifths rule. Theories: Crenshaw's intersectionality and the Rawlsian principle of distributive justice frame bias and fairness. AN_Task None: method survey without a professional application task.

fields.AN_Notes: Practice guide for small and medium-sized enterprises with the KI-FAIRNESS framework for fair prompting. Prompting roles: recommended practice, learning content (fair prompting as a new skill), and research instrument for the authors' own image-generation probes with DALL-E 2 and Midjourney (Section 5.1). Techniques: prompt element 'Rolle' (Role_Persona), examples of the desired style (ICL), and General_Guidance with the concrete strategies verbatim: 'Am besten ist es daher, Prompts auf Englisch zu formulieren und in die Beschreibung explizit die gewünschte Darstellung von weiblichen und männlichen Chef*innen aufzunehmen'; 'Es könnte z.B. explizit gefordert werden, dass Frauen und Männer, Menschen unterschiedlicher Hautfarbe und sozialer Schicht dargestellt werden sollen'; gender neutrality and a 'Verwirrungstaktik' naming both genders for reference letters; anonymisation. Bias axes come from the authors' own image probes (gender, skin colour, age, slimness, absence of disabled persons, privileged office settings) and the worked example of sexualised depiction of women and especially Women of Color (Intersectional). Indirect_Discrimination: job-ad wording that appeals to men, reproduced by a model trained on earlier ads, disadvantages women applicants. Demonstrated: adding the word 'divers' to a prompt was tried and changed little; the probes are illustrative, not a completed assessment. Further stages proposed: data diversity (Pre_Processing), targeted training of models with gender-inclusive terms (In_Training), governance, training and human review (Organisational_Process). AN_Task Other_Task: drafting job advertisements and reference letters and generating images for company communication. AN_Population Not_SW_Specific: company staff and managers outside social work. Gender is not defined; the gender star and a mention of genderqueer people in the data gap do not enter the analysis categories, which treat gender together with skin colour. 'Feministische KI' and Data Feminism are named as outlook and further reading and do not frame the analysis, so AN_Theory_Reference is No.
